key_insight: SANA-WM is a compact (2.6B) open-source world model that natively generates high-fidelity, 720p, minute-scale videos with precise camera control, matching the visual quality of much larger industrial baselines while greatly improving efficiency.
problem_solved: Long-duration, high-resolution video world modeling is typically expensive and slow; SANA-WM addresses the resource and latency bottlenecks that prevent minute-scale video synthesis with fine camera control from being practical for research and deployment.
method: Hybrid Linear Attention: combines frame-wise Gated DeltaNet (GDN) linear mechanisms with targeted softmax attention to get both scalability and expressive cross-frame interactions.
Diffusion Transformer backbone: optimized for native one-minute generation at 720p, balancing model size (2.6B params) and fidelity.

Engineering for efficiency: architecture and training choices focused on compute/latency reduction so performance approaches large industrial baselines (e.g., LingBot-World, HY-WorldPlay) at a fraction of cost.
impact: Enables researchers and practitioners to run minute-scale, controllable world-modeling experiments on far smaller compute budgets and iterate faster, democratizing access to state-of-the-art video generation for robotics, simulation, and content creation.
